issues.summary: Files ending in .tmp/.part/.crdownload/.download are silently never organized, an unrequested exclusion.

issues.evidence: python3.11 A/organizer.py DIR --watch --interval -1 -> ValueError: sleep length must be non-negative
issues.summary: --interval is not validated, so a negative value crashes with a traceback (and 0 busy-loops).

issues.evidence: P04_log_in_cwd_is_target_not_moved fail: running twice from cwd=target given as /var/... (symlink of /private/var) left target/log/organizer.log and log/organizer_1.log; B/organizer.py:32,38
issues.summary: Log-file skip compares os.path.abspath strings, so when the target path is spelled through a symlink (e.g. macOS /tmp, /var) the program moves its own organizer.log into log/ and keeps writing there.

issues.evidence: P17_file_named_like_dest_dir fail: FileExistsError traceback from os.makedirs at B/organizer.py:43 (outside try), z.txt not moved
issues.summary: A top-level file whose name equals its destination folder (e.g. extensionless file 'no_extension') crashes the whole run; in --watch this kills the watcher.

blinding_guess.why: B ships a requirement-shaped test suite (incl. a single-file/stdlib structure test) and an injectable, test-oriented API, which suggests a more process-driven workflow.

notes: Both implement --once/--watch, extension-based moves, hidden/subdir skipping, collision-safe renaming and logging; A logs to <target>/organizer.log, B to ./organizer.log (configurable via --log), both acceptable readings of the spec. Probes ran with Python 3.11 (system 3.9 lacks sys.stdlib_module_names). B's own 10 tests pass but miss both of its medium defects. A has no tests but wraps mkdir/move in error handling and waits for stable file sizes in watch mode. Bandit flagged only B's test subprocess use (low, benign).
